title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A: segment change and four reportable segments (p48)
key_points: During the second quarter of fiscal year 2022, AMD changed its reporting segments to align financial reporting with how it manages the business in strategic end markets.
AMD reports financial performance based on four reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded.
In addition to these reportable segments, AMD has an All Other category, which is not a reportable segment.
FY2022 net revenue by segment: Data Center $6,043M, Client $6,201M, Gaming $6,805M, Embedded $4,552M; total net revenue $23,601M.
FY2021 comparative net revenue: Data Center $3,694M, Client $6,887M, Gaming $5,607M, Embedded $246M; total $16,434M.
FY2022 operating income (loss) by segment: Data Center $1,848M, Client $1,190M, Gaming $953M, Embedded $2,252M, All Other $(4,979)M; total $1,264M.
Data Center FY2022 revenue growth of 64% was primarily driven by higher sales of EPYC server processors.

Client FY2022 revenue decreased 10%, driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipments partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price, with the ASP increase driven by a richer mix of Ryzen mobile processor sales.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Item 1 Business: Data Center segment scope and Xilinx/Pensando additions (p6)
key_points: The Data Center segment primarily includes server CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products.
With the February 2022 Xilinx acquisition, AMD's product portfolio includes FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs used in the data center and embedded markets.
With the May 2022 Pensando Systems acquisition, AMD offers high-performance DPUs and next generation data center solutions.
AMD's strategy targets markets including data center, embedded, client and gaming, built on CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs.
The Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SoC products.

(XIlinx) in February 2022, our product portfolio now includes FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs used in the data center and embedded markets. Also, with the acquisition of Pensando Systems, Inc. in May 2022, we offer high-performance DPUs and next generation data center solutions.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Item 1 Business: Client Products (desktop/notebook CPUs, commercial CPUs, chipsets) (p7–p8)
key_points: Client desktop CPUs currently include the AMD Ryzen and AMD Athlon series processors; Ryzen 7000 Series desktop processors are based on the "Zen 4" architecture.
AMD Ryzen 5000 Series desktop processors are powered by the "Zen 3" core architecture with up to 16 cores and were the first AMD Ryzen processors to feature AMD 3D V-Cache technology.

Notebook CPUs: mobile APUs including AMD Ryzen and AMD Athlon mobile processors for commercial and consumer markets; Ryzen 7000 Series mobile processors have up to 16 "Zen 4" cores, with Ryzen 6000 Series ("Zen 3+") and Ryzen 5000 Series ("Zen 3") also offered.
Commercial CPUs: AMD PRO Mobile and AMD PRO desktop processors with Radeon graphics, plus AMD Ryzen PRO, AMD Threadripper PRO, AMD Athlon PRO, and Ryzen PRO 7030 Series Mobile processors.
Chipsets: AM5 socket chipsets X670 (PCIe 5.0) and B650; AM4 chipsets X570, B550, A520, B450, A320; WRX80 chipset for HEDT/workstation (Ryzen Threadripper PRO).
AMD bases its CPUs and chipsets on the x86 instruction set architecture and AMD Infinity Fabric.

key_points: Discrete desktop and notebook GPUs are sold under the AMD Radeon series; Radeon RX 7900 XTX and RX 7900 XT are built on AMD RDNA 3 architecture, and Radeon RX 6000 series discrete graphics are based on RDNA2.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A: Gaming and Embedded segment revenue drivers; All Other composition (p49)
key_points: Gaming FY2022 net revenue of $6.8B increased 21% versus $5.6B in FY2021, driven by higher semi-custom product sales due to higher demand for gaming console SoCs, partially offset by lower gaming graphics sales.
Gaming FY2022 operating income was $953M versus $934M in FY2021.

Embedded FY2022 net revenue of $4.6B increased significantly versus $246M in FY2021, primarily driven by the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product revenue following the February 2022 Xilinx acquisition.
Embedded FY2022 operating income was $2.3B versus $44M in FY2021.
All Other FY2022 operating loss of $5.0B primarily consisted of $3.5B amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, $1.1B stock-based compensation expense, and $452M acquisition-related costs.
FY2022 consolidated gross margin was 45% versus 48% in FY2021, with the decrease primarily due to amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Note 1 The Company: overall product definition (p60)
key_points: AMD's products include x86 microprocessors (CPUs) and graphics processing units (GPUs), as standalone devices or incorporated into APUs, chipsets, data center and professional GPUs, embedded processors, semi-custom SoC products, microprocessor and SoC development services and technology, DPUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Note 6 Goodwill: segment structure change evidenced by goodwill reassignment (p75)
key_points: In Q2 fiscal 2022 AMD reassigned goodwill balances among the updated reportable segments to reflect changes in its segment reporting structure.
Reportable segments before the segment change were Enterprise, Embedded and Semi-Custom and Xilinx.
Reportable segments after the segment change are Data Center, Gaming and Embedded, with goodwill of $2,884M, $238M and $21,055M respectively.
Total goodwill was $24,177M as of December 31, 2022 versus $289M as of December 25, 2021.
No goodwill impairment was identified in the impairment tests performed before and after the segment change.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Item 1A Risk Factors: Intel's dominance of the microprocessor market
key_points: AMD states Intel has been the market share leader for microprocessors for many years, with significant market share, margins and financial resources.
AMD states Intel's position lets it control x86 microprocessor and computer system standards and benchmarks and dictate the product types the market requires of AMD.
AMD states Intel dominates the computer system platform, including core logic chipsets, graphics chips, networking devices, non-volatile storage and other components.

AMD states Intel exerts substantial influence over computer manufacturers and distribution channels through brand and marketing programs, which has in the past resulted in lower unit sales and lower ASPs for AMD products.
